nodes.text: AI is designed, governed and used so that it strengthens cooperation and flourishing at the individual, organisational, societal and planetary scales, rather than extracting from them.

sources.author: atkins-wilson
sources.title: Evolving Prosocial AI · How We Shape the Systems that Shape AI - and Us
sources.description: A 67-page manuscript by Paul Atkins and David Sloan Wilson of ProSocial World, version of 28 June 2026, accepted for Cambridge Elements in Applied Evolutionary Science. It argues that worldviews, acting as cultural replicators, set the selection pressures that decide whether AI extracts from or strengthens cooperation at individual, organisational, societal and planetary scales, and proposes Ostrom’s core design principles as the institutional answer. An earlier draft of 6 March 2026 was circulated on Substack; this later version supersedes it. Page numbers refer to the PDF.

goal.title: Flourishing at every scale
goal.summary: The authors judge AI by its effects on people, organisations, societies and the planet. Each scale has its own conditions, drawn from Section 4.

goal.title: Make cooperation pay
goal.summary: The authors' central claim: prosocial AI needs institutions that reward cooperation, not heroic sacrifice. Ostrom's core design principles, applied to AI, are the proposed conditions; worldviews come with them.

current_reality.title: The book's starting point
current_reality.summary: Three claims from the book's framework that frame everything else. They are attributed observations with no causal connections drawn.

current_reality.title: What gets rewarded
current_reality.summary: Four extractive worldviews, held in place by power and training and amplified by temporal discounting, shape what institutions reward and so what gets built.

current_reality.title: Harms at every scale
current_reality.summary: From people's eroded capabilities to firms that outgrow more careful rivals, public systems that harm without accountability and costs pushed onto the planet. Candidate causes, not established findings.

current_reality.title: The cancer pattern and the trap
current_reality.summary: Weakened institutions cannot govern what weakens them, eroded users depend more, and prosocial alternatives start behind: together, a social trap.

conflict.title: Keep up, or avoid harm?
conflict.summary: A firm building AI needs to keep up with rivals that optimise for engagement, and to avoid harming its users. The authors' answer is to change the institutions, not to ask for sacrifice.

conflict.title: Let it do the work, or keep the skill?
conflict.summary: A person wants work done quickly and wants to keep their own capabilities. The authors describe living this tension themselves while writing the book.

future_reality.title: Make prosocial AI pay
future_reality.summary: Design principles, procurement, measurement and visible energy costs could turn prosocial AI from a handicap into an advantage. The authors' own caution about imposing principles is kept as a risk.

future_reality.title: Build capability, not dependence
future_reality.summary: AI that scaffolds thinking and honours stated preferences could leave people more capable and more demanding of good tools. Mixed evidence is kept as a risk.

future_reality.title: Shared ground and shared value
future_reality.summary: Bridging algorithms and deliberation, and ownership models that share value with contributors, with the timing limit of fact-checks kept in view.

future_reality.title: How prosocial worldviews spread
future_reality.summary: Demonstrations, networks and stories spread prosocial worldviews through ordinary social learning. With the other changes, success at each scale could reinforce the rest.

prerequisite.title: Measure, test and fund independently
prerequisite.summary: The authors' own limits: no agreed measure of capability impact, evidence that skews Western and democratic, and research funded by the industry it studies.

prerequisite.title: Build the backing
prerequisite.summary: Extraction has far more resources, training reproduces it and many prosocial models are still niche. Procurement, education and rigorous demonstrations are the proposed answers.

overview.title: How worldviews shape AI, and AI shapes us
overview.text: Atkins and Wilson treat worldviews as cultural replicators that spread through what they reward. AI systems carry those worldviews in their behaviour and teach them back to the people around them, at a moment when human cooperation is still a partial evolutionary transition. These cards reconstruct that framework before the AI’s practical map.
link: Read the framework and what stands in the way →

overview.title: Flourishing at every scale, with cooperation that pays
overview.text: People, organisations, societies and the planet each need AI that builds rather than extracts. Underneath, institutions have to make cooperation more rewarding than extraction; the book proposes Ostrom’s core design principles for that.
link: Inspect the goal and its conditions →

overview.title: Extraction that rewards itself
overview.text: Four extractive worldviews and the pull of immediate rewards shape what institutions reward. AI built to capture attention and do tasks for people erodes their capabilities, firms that externalise harm outgrow the rest, and a social trap locks the pattern in.

overview.title: Two dilemmas, for a firm and for a person
overview.text: A firm has to keep up with rivals and avoid harming its users; a person wants work done quickly and wants to keep their own skills. Both are proposed readings of the book, offered for real cases to test.

overview.title: Make prosocial AI pay, and build capability
overview.text: Apply the design principles, require capability audits in procurement, measure capability impacts and design AI to scaffold thinking. The authors’ own cautions, such as imposing principles over local wisdom, are kept as risks.
link: See the proposed changes and their risks →

overview.title: Measures, wider tests and real backing
overview.text: Drawn from the authors’ own limits: an agreed measure of capability impact, tests beyond Western and democratic settings, independent research funding and demonstrations at scale. These are proposed conditions, not completed work.
link: Review the obstacles and intermediate objectives →

overview.title: Researchers, technologists, policymakers, funders
overview.text: The book closes by naming what each group could do. Here they are as an illustrative sequence; the existing conditions are examples and nobody is assigned.

overview.title: The cancer pattern and the life pattern
overview.text: The book reads AI through multilevel selection: when success at a lower level comes at the expense of the levels above, the result looks like a tumour; when success at each level supports the others, it looks like life. Its claim is that institutions, not virtue, decide which pattern AI follows, and that the next few years matter most.

overview.title: Paul Atkins and David Sloan Wilson’s Evolving Prosocial AI
overview.text: The argument is Paul Atkins and David Sloan Wilson’s, from their book accepted for Cambridge Elements in Applied Evolutionary Science. The AI is responsible for selecting, paraphrasing and connecting the material. Every item has a page reference and a labelled basis; source credit is not author endorsement.
